minutes.headline: Sewer commission asked a developer to study Kimball and Hollis roads before approving a private extension on Pawn Street.
minutes.summary: The commission, meeting in person for the first time in about a year and a half, heard an engineer and developer propose a roughly 939-foot privately funded sewer extension along a street shoulder. Members preferred a route serving more properties, so the engineer will work with the DPW director and the town will send a letter to residents on the alternate streets. Routine business included a contract extension signature, a favorable budget review, minutes, and scheduling.

what_happened.line: The commission asked for Kimball and Hollis roads to be evaluated as an alternative to a private sewer extension proposed on Pawn Street.
The engineer will work with the DPW director on routing down Kimball or Hollis, with stubs left for future connections.
The town will send residents on Hollis and Kimball a letter with a firm response deadline asking whether they want sewer.
Under the developer's plan the extension would be privately built and the main given to the town, which would collect tie-in fees later.
Members found the FY21 budget in line and revenues above what was anticipated; a one-year contract extension was passed down for signature.

why_it_matters: Residents on Kimball and Hollis roads may be asked whether they want a sewer connection, and a reply to the town's letter could shape who is served and who pays tie-in fees.
A privately funded main handed to the town becomes a public asset the sewer system maintains, so the route chosen decides how many properties it serves and what the town takes on.
watch_next: The letter to Hollis and Kimball residents and its response deadline.
A future agenda item on the sewer maintenance program.
